blurb:
Boxer meets Corgi and the result is exactly as chaotic and charming as you'd expect. Asher is a three-year-old, 40-pound ginger brindle goofball who the shelter volunteers describe as "funny" — and based on everything they say about him, that tracks. He's playful, expressive, and will absolutely bring the ball back to you as long as you keep throwing it. He went through the Mostly Mutts Prison Pups training program, so he comes with real skills and a handler who can walk you through exactly how to introduce him to new situations.

He's got some personality quirks worth knowing upfront. He shouldn't live with another dog — he's guarded toys and beds from them in the past — and cats are a no. He also gets excited around small kids, so a home with teenagers 15 and up would be the right fit. He's vocal and has opinions, so an apartment isn't really his scene. But if you've got a house with a fenced yard and some room to run? He's going to thrive.

He's in a foster home right now doing great, even entertaining himself inside on his own. His foster family says he'd make a solid office dog, which honestly makes him sound like a better coworker than most people. Submit an inquiry through Mostly Mutts and go meet him — his trainer will be there to answer everything.
scoring_notes:
• Boxer-Corgi mix with a Prison Pups credential is a genuinely rare and visually irresistible combination for readers
• 'Funny' volunteer descriptor plus the office-dog anecdote give editors a ready-made headline moment
• Specific household requirements narrow the pool but also sharpen urgency for the exact right adopter

blurb:
Josie has floppy ears, a nubby little tail, and enough energy to make a previous adopter return her after a couple of months because they couldn't keep up. She's not embarrassed about that. Some dogs just need the right match, and Josie knows who she is. She's six years old, 35 pounds, and rates herself a 5 to 7 on the energy scale with occasional zoomies. That's honest self-reporting and you have to respect it.

She graduated from the Mostly Mutts Prison Pups program, so she's got real training behind her. On walks she's engaged and fun. Back home she'll find the couch and park herself next to you. She does some mouthy, playful nibbling during play — nothing aggressive, just her way of engaging — so older kids around 10 and up would be a better fit than little ones. No other dogs, no cats.

She relaxed enough during her shelter bath that she was giving kisses by the time they got to her ears. That tells you a lot about who she is underneath the energy. She's in foster now and ready to meet you. Head over to Mostly Mutts and ask about Josie.
scoring_notes:
• Returned once but self-aware and unbothered — the 'knows who she is' framing is instantly shareable and voice-driven
• The bath-time kisses detail is a single vivid image that does more emotional work than a full paragraph
• Prison Pups grad with honest energy self-reporting gives cautious adopters the transparency they need to say yes

blurb:
Bolton came into Mostly Mutts underweight, thin-coated, and clearly coming off a rough stretch. That's behind him now. He's nine years old, 64 pounds, and by all accounts a completely different dog from the one who walked through those doors. His foster family describes him as someone who "lights up every room he walks into," which is not a small thing for a dog who had to earn that energy back.

He's a hound-boxer mix, so his nose runs the show on walks. He sniffs everything, investigates everything, and seems genuinely delighted by the world around him. He's also got a goofy side — his favorite move with other dogs is a game of tag where he runs at them and then bolts, hoping they'll chase him. It works. He went through the Prison Pups training program, loves kids around 8 to 12, and is good with other friendly dogs.

No cats, and toddlers would be a little too small for him to navigate safely around. But if you've got a family with school-age kids and a dog who'd love a running buddy, Bolton might be the one to go meet. Senior dogs with this kind of personality and warmth don't stay available long. Visit Mostly Mutts and ask for Bolton.
scoring_notes:
• Came in underweight and depleted, now lights up every room — one of the strongest physical and emotional transformation arcs on this list
• Senior hound-boxer with Prison Pups training and a goofy tag-playing personality is a standout newsletter story
• Nine-year-old dogs face the steepest adoption odds; the blurb itself flags urgency, making this a high-impact feature candidate

shelter_name: Mostly Mutts Animal Rescue & Adoption, Inc.
blurb:
Twiggy had a home for years after being adopted from Mostly Mutts. Then another cat joined the household, the two didn't get along, and her world flipped upside down. She's about seven years old, around 12 pounds, and a tortoiseshell. She showed up at the shelter a little spicy, which is completely fair given what she'd just been through.

She's been decompressing in a foster home and opening up. Once she knows you, she loves attention from people. She's litter trained, current on her vaccines, spayed, microchipped, and combo tested negative. The people at Mostly Mutts are still learning more about her as she settles in, so her profile will keep filling out.

She'd do best as the only cat in the home. That's the one clear thing her previous owner flagged, and it's worth taking seriously. On dogs, it would depend on the individual dog and how cat-savvy they are. Kids are welcome as long as they give her space to come to them on her own terms.

She's not a mystery. She's just a cat who got uprooted after years of stability and needs someone patient enough to let her land. The adoption fee is $175. She's with Mostly Mutts in Kennesaw. Reach out by phone or email to meet her.
scoring_notes:
• A seven-year-old tortoiseshell with years of home life lost to a household conflict — deeply relatable and emotionally compelling
• Still decompressing and profile still filling out, signaling a recent intake but a layered story worth following
• Patient, solo-cat home is a clear ask that helps the right reader self-select and act quickly

shelter_name: Mostly Mutts Animal Rescue & Adoption, Inc.
blurb:
Iceman was adopted from Mostly Mutts as a kitten. He had a family for five years. Then things changed for them, and he ended up back at the rescue through no fault of his own. He's 11 pounds now, fully grown, and settling into a foster home while he waits for his next chapter.

He's a hang-with-you kind of cat. Not needy, not aloof. He likes being around his people and watching the world go by. He was great with four kids in a previous foster placement, so a family with children who know how to be calm around cats should work out fine. On other cats, he's done best without other males around. A female cat roommate could be a good fit, but it would take a proper introduction to find out.

He's neutered, microchipped, up to date on vaccines, and combo tested negative. The adoption fee is $175. He's located in Kennesaw with Mostly Mutts, and you can reach them by phone or email to get started. Given that he's already proven he knows how to be a good houseguest, whoever adopts him is getting a pretty easy transition.
scoring_notes:
• Five years of proven family life makes him one of the lowest-risk adult cat adoptions on this list
• Returned through no fault of his own — a clean, sympathetic backstory with broad reader appeal
• Fully vetted and family-tested with a straightforward $175 fee, removing friction for serious adopters

shelter_name: Mostly Mutts Animal Rescue & Adoption, Inc.
blurb:
She came in with her siblings as part of the Go-Gos litter, got adopted, and then life got complicated. Gina is about 11 months old, weighs around five pounds, and has a stomach that doesn't always cooperate. She was returned after a month because of ongoing gastrointestinal issues, and after months of vet visits and food adjustments, she's doing better, though the vomiting hasn't fully gone away and nobody's figured out exactly why yet.

Here's the thing though. Her foster calls her the best cat ever. She's playful, snuggly, and pretty independent. She stayed small and probably always will, so if you've ever wanted a cat that keeps a little of that kitten energy permanently, Gina is it. She gets along with the adult cats in her foster home and met a dog on leash without flinching.

Because she eats a special diet, she'd do best as an only cat, or in a home where feeding can be done separately so she stays on her food. She's already proven she can make it work with other cats if the situation is right. Just something to plan for. Kids are welcome as long as they're gentle with her.

Gina is at Mostly Mutts in Kennesaw. Call or email to set up a meet. She's been waiting for the right person, and her foster is pretty convinced that person is out there.
scoring_notes:
• Foster calls her 'the best cat ever' — a rare, quotable endorsement that builds instant reader trust
• Returned once due to GI issues but now stabilized, creating a redemption arc that resonates emotionally
• Months of vet visits and food trials suggest an extended wait that gives this story real urgency
